title: Store line: a struct's missing field is reported before trailing characters (OQ-136 follow-up)
description: Oracle: a store line `{"id":"proj-a1"} X` is refused with `Invalid JSON at line 1: missing field `title` at line 1 column 16` (exit 7): serde_json deserializes the object and checks its required fields when the object closes, BEFORE it looks for trailing characters. The port reports `trailing characters at line 1 column 18` first (before 2026-09-24 it said `expected value`, also wrong). Fix: in the store decoder (port/core/decode.bend, json.bend members), defer the trailing-characters verdict of the members split until the record's field checks have run. Add a case with a hand-written fixture (e.g. `error_jsonl_missing_then_trailing`), capture, amend S2.27. Found by the OQ-136 probe battery (scratch mb/raw.jsonl).

title: Quantified laws the spec names (label normalization, count conservation, comparator orders)

Why: of 61 laws only the scaffold's `fast_is_spec` is quantified; the other 60 are closed facts about one value each, so the law side of the project's two equivalences is mostly unbuilt. What: state and prove, over all inputs: label normalization is idempotent; the `count --by-*` groups sum to the total; each list comparator is a total order. Keep the checker's cost in mind: no law may make it normalize a large Peano Nat (a biased Nat OOM-killed PROOF at 16 GB on 2026-09-23). Done when: the laws are proved and cited on the parity board.

title: JS lane faults on a record with a long text member (>= 64 KB)
description: Found 2026-09-24 while timing real store copies. On the JS lane (bun, bn16.js of the working tree after 9fa7e2f; bn11.js of b25ac04 behaves the same) `count` aborts with 'bend: memory fault (machine stack overflow?)' on a one-record store whose description is 64 KB or 256 KB; 16 KB answers. Real stores hit it: music_theory_data_tool (25 MB, longest line 168,961 bytes) and hedge_fund_data_tool (46 MB, longest line 1,333,436 bytes) fault; historical_soldiers (1.1 MB) answers. The C lanes answer all of them. DISC-008 (RESOLVED) covered store SIZE (many records), not one long string: this is the same runtime structure walk (a String is nested constructors, walked on the JS call stack) reached by a single member. Next: find the def that walks a string non-tail-recursively on the decode/render path (candidates: the JSON string lexer, String.eq/++ over the whole member, the escape/unescape), probe it under port/probes/, and either make it accumulator-shaped or amend DISC-008 with this threshold. Probe stores: scratchpad longline/k16,k64,k256 built from goldens/fixtures/large.jsonl line 1 plus a description of repeated 'word '.

title: Profile the load path and remove the quadratic duplicate-id check
description:
Why: every command loads the whole store; batch 5 added `Store.has_id`, which scans the records loaded so far for every new record (quadratic). The decode of the 44-member record, `Model.repaired` and the BLOCKED relation's fixed point are the other suspects. What: profile a C build on the 1 MB and 25 MB copies (perf, or the keep-audit of the bend2 skill), rank the hotspots, and replace the duplicate check with an id index built once per load. A new fast def is a Phase 5 lever: it needs its spec twin, a `{fast == spec}` law and the BEADS_RUST_SPEC=1 kill-switch. Done when: the hotspot table is in perf/ and the duplicate check is linear, with lanes and PROOF green.
